about: Three-Way Domain Expansion is a manga spread from Jujutsu Kaisen in which three sorcerers declare their Domain Expansions at the same time. On the left, the burly Ryu Ishigori screams with his mouth wide open; in the middle, a battered Yuta Okkotsu raises his hand in a hand sign with a quiet, focused face; on the right, Takako Uro shouts with wild, round eyes. Each has a blank speech bubble where the domain name would be. The template labels three parties who all go all-in on their own answer at the exact same moment, usually to show that none of them will back down.
origin: The page comes from Gege Akutami's Jujutsu Kaisen manga, in the Culling Game arc, during the battle at the Sendai Colony. In the story the three domains clash and cancel each other out, which is part of why fans reuse it for arguments where nobody wins.
usage:
There are three boxes, one in each speech bubble. Fill them left to right with three rival answers to the same question: Ishigori's loud bubble, Yuta's narrow middle bubble, and Uro's on the right. Short phrases fit best since the bubbles are small.

It works for any three-way standoff: three teammates calling different strategies, three fandoms arguing about the best season, three coworkers proposing three different tools. The funniest version makes the third option a dismissive "just use X" that ends the debate.
